source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It removes maternal anti-D antibodies that have already caused fetal hemolysis.","B":"It changes fetal Rh antigen expression for the remainder of pregnancy.","C":"It helps prevent maternal Rh immunization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal red cells.","D":"The 28-week dose generally replaces postpartum prophylaxis if the pregnancy remains uncomplicated and maternal antibody screening stays negative."}}
source_row.rationale: Rho(D) immune globulin provides passive anti-D that suppresses maternal immunization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal red cells. It prevents sensitization; it does not treat established fetal hemolytic disease or change fetal Rh type. Antepartum prophylaxis does not automatically eliminate postpartum dosing when the newborn is Rh-positive.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed RhoGAM Ultra-Filtered PLUS label — Indications/Usage and obstetric dosing: prevention of Rh immunization, routine antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks and postpartum prophylaxis when indicated. Current FDA RhoGAM label at the exact DailyMed set ID; live version rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies; medication administration, adverse effects/interactions and monitoring. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: An unsensitized Rh(D)-negative pregnant client receives Rho(D) immune globulin at 28 weeks. Which explanation best describes the purpose of this therapy?
